judgments.forked_readings_summary:
All four readings describe the same task with no material fork on any axis.

SCOPE BOUNDARY (full agreement): All four name exactly one read-only, synchronous endpoint GET /v1/users/{userId}/export that emits the authenticated caller's OWN four profile fields {id, email, displayName, createdAt} as a CSV download, gated by a self-only auth check (token subject must equal {userId}, else 403). All four explicitly draw the boundary at self-export of profile-only data and exclude admin/bulk, alternate formats, related records, and async/job machinery.

SURFACES IN SCOPE (full agreement): All four list the same surfaces — route/controller handler, self-match authorization check (403 on mismatch), CSV serialization of the four fixed fields with header row + RFC-4180-style escaping, text/csv + Content-Disposition: attachment;filename headers, and the read path against the existing user store. Readings 2, 3, and 4 explicitly list tests; reading 1 omits tests from its surface list but this is a minor detail, not a scope difference.

SURFACES OUT OF SCOPE (full agreement): All four exclude admin/bulk multi-user export, non-CSV formats (JSON/PDF/XLSX), related records (orders/sessions), background/async jobs and polling, new auth infrastructure (reuse existing bearer auth, add only the self-match check), and pagination/streaming. Reading 4 additionally names rate limiting/caching/export-history, but these fall naturally within the others' "no extra features" stance — an elaboration, not a fork.

CORE BEHAVIOR (full agreement): Identical across all four — authenticated caller requesting their own userId gets 200 with a one-row text/csv attachment of the four fields; cross-user (mismatched token subject) gets 403 and no profile data emitted.

The only deltas are trivia: reading 1 doesn't list tests as a surface; reading 2 adds an explicit 401 unauthenticated test and a 404-not-found read case; reading 4 adds rate-limiting/caching to the exclusion list. None of these alter scope, surfaces, or behavior at the level of meaning.

All four readings describe an identical task: a single read-only, synchronous endpoint GET /v1/users/{userId}/export that returns the authenticated caller's OWN profile as a CSV-attachment download. Every axis converges:

- Scope boundary: all four agree on exactly one endpoint, self-export-of-profile-only, with a self-ownership auth check (bearer token subject must equal {userId}, else 403). All four explicitly exclude admin/bulk, alternate formats, related records, and async/job machinery.
- Surfaces in scope: all four list the same set — route/controller handler, the self-match authorization check (403 on mismatch), the existing user read path for the single {userId}, CSV serialization of the exact four fields {id, email, displayName, createdAt} with header row + one data row and RFC-4180-style escaping, and the text/csv + Content-Disposition: attachment;filename headers. Three of four also explicitly call out tests (self 200 vs cross-user 403, CSV shape/escaping).
- Surfaces out of scope: identical lists — no admin/bulk multi-user export, no JSON/PDF/XLSX, no related records (orders/sessions/etc.), no background/async/polling, no new auth infrastructure (reuse existing bearer auth, add only the self-match), no pagination/streaming/rate-limiting.
- Core behavior: all four agree — authenticated self request returns 200 with a CSV attachment of the four fields; cross-user/mismatched token returns 403 and emits nothing.

The only differences are trivial detail-level variations, none of which change the task: reading #2 adds an explicit 401-unauthenticated test case and a 404-not-found read path; reading #4 adds extra out-of-scope examples (caching headers, export-history persistence, signed-URL delivery). These are elaborations within the same scope, not forks. No reading disagrees about an endpoint, a surface, a format, or the auth semantics.

All four readings describe the identical task: one read-only, synchronous GET /v1/users/{userId}/export endpoint that returns the authenticated caller's OWN four profile fields (id, email, displayName, createdAt) as a single-row text/csv attachment, gated by a self-match auth check (bearer-token subject must equal {userId}, else 403). Scope boundary ("self-export of profile-only data"), in-scope surfaces (route/controller handler, self-match authz, CSV serialization with header row + RFC-4180 escaping, text/csv + Content-Disposition: attachment headers, reuse of the existing user read path), out-of-scope surfaces (no admin/bulk export, no alternate formats like JSON/PDF/XLSX, no related records, no async/job machinery, no new auth infra, no pagination/streaming), and core behavior (self → 200 CSV; cross-user → 403, emit nothing) all match across the four. The only differences are detail-level elaborations, not forks: reading 1 omits tests as an explicit surface (readings 2/3/4 list them), and readings 2/4 additionally spell out the 401-unauthenticated and 404-not-found edge cases that the others leave implicit.
